messages:
maya: FYI apiserver started returning 429s around 13:02 UTC for the gpu-provisioner namespace. QPS spiked to ~1.1k for ~4m. controller-manager queue climbed to ~420 pending reconciles. :eyes:

oliver: saw same. traces show a tight loop inside the provisioner: it's replaying a shim-resume path whenever a GPU node attaches. each replay issues ~10 writes to the API per attach event.

maya: exact log snippet: `provisioner: shim replay triggered for attachID=shm-9a3f; enqueued 12 reconcile ops`

kai: is this the shim replay patch we landed last week? thought we debounced it.

oliver: that debounce only applied to successful attach events. the error path still triggers immediate replay. race with node Ready transition.

julia: short-term mitigation = throttling the provisioner to avoid bursting the apiserver. can we flip a feature-gate to add a client-side rate limiter?

ramon: staging change ready: set PROVISIONER_REPLAY_WINDOW_MS=1200 and add `--max-requests=50` env. rolling it to canary now.

maya: also seeing apiserver metric spikes: `apiserver_current_inflight_requests` jumped and `apiserver_request_latencies_seconds_bucket{verb="POST"}` shifted. adding a temporary reject policy for noisy reconciles might help.

kai: long term we should upstream a guard in the shim code: dedupe by attachID + short TTL, don't enqueue if identical replay already pending.

oliver: agree. also discussing controller-manager flags: drop `--concurrent-reconciles` from 20 -> 8 for gpu-controller to reduce tail latency.

julia: small awk script to identify offending controllers: `kubectl get events -A --field-selector reason=ShimReplay | awk '{print $1,$2,$5}'` — will share in the thread.

ramon: canary patch vel rolled at 13:20, metrics look improved in canary. apiserver 429 rate down ~80% for that shard. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks. we'll keep the global fallback (route-to-standby) open if things regress. tagging infra-oncall.

sre-bot: INC-2026-3423 created (controlplane: shim-replay burst causing apiserver throttling). Severity: P2.

kai: checklist for follow-up: 1) hotfix debounce on error path (oliver), 2) controller-manager concurrency change (julia), 3) dedupe in shim (design doc), 4) add circuit-breaker on provisioner client (ramon).

oliver: putting a short RFC in #eng-ml for the shim dedupe approach. will link here.

maya: anyone see cost impact? GPU attach loops will cause extra protos and write ops (billing note). we should estimate extra token of control-plane ops for last week.

ramon: preliminary: ~0.6% API request increase during the window, negligible $ but risk of outages higher.

julia: rolling back the specific patch if the canary had issues is ready but not necessary now. we should still schedule the rollback window.

maya: good. closing the loop: if 429s reappear escalate to P1. otherwise follow the checklist and track RFC. thanks all. :pray:
